name: Phantaveil
description: Phantaveil exploits the hypnagogic threshold — the liminal state between wakefulness and sleep — by pharmacologically extending and stabilizing it into a prolonged altered consciousness that is neither sleep nor waking. Users remain in a deeply relaxed, perceptually rich state for 2-4 hours in which hallucinations are vivid but controllable, thought is fluid and associative, and the usual barriers between conscious and subconscious processing dissolve. Nightshade markets it as a 'creative cognition supplement' but its primary use is recreational and its secondary use is interrogation-adjacent.
effects: Dissolved boundary between conscious and subconscious thought
Profound sense of interconnection and insight
side_effects: Disorienting transition to normal sleep or wakefulness
Content of hallucinations can turn distressing without warning
Reduced psychological defensiveness makes users susceptible to suggestion and manipulation
Occasional failure to transition to actual sleep — users remain in state for dangerous extended periods
BCI input during Phantaveil state causes extreme sensory overload
duration: 2-4 hours hypnagogic state, transitions to normal sleep or wakefulness
cultural_context: Phantaveil occupies a strange cultural space — it's too controlled to be fully recreational, too experiential to be clinical, and its dual-use profile (the reduced defensiveness makes it a preferred tool for coercive information extraction when combined with the right questioning techniques) keeps it perpetually on the edge of being reclassified as illegal. Artists, philosophers, and people engaged in intensive therapy use it legitimately. Fixers and people with worse intentions use it for other purposes entirely, which Nightshade is careful never to acknowledge officially.
story_hooks: A witness to something important was dosed with Phantaveil and questioned — they don't know what they revealed or to whom, and the crew needs to figure out what information was extracted before whoever took it acts on it.

A Tier 3 therapy collective has been using Phantaveil in group sessions, claiming breakthrough results for trauma processing — but several participants have developed identical false memories of an event that never happened, and the therapist running the sessions has disappeared.
